answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down. Shuffle the 9 Conflict II cards and deal 5 face down on top. Shuffle the 3 Conflict I cards and deal 1 face down on top. This makes a 10-card deck with 1 I, 5 II, and 4 III; return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In a four-player game, a player starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game, at 0 VP. In either game the player has 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 3 troops in their garrison, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent (your Swordmaster) next to the game board’; score marker is on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; place three troops in a garrison; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. On a Reveal turn, reveal the cards still in hand and resolve only their Reveal boxes, not the boxes of cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you, from both kinds of turns, to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal Turn: effects are from ‘just-revealed cards only’; Clean Up moves ‘all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. You must be able to pay a space cost immediately before resolving effects from either the space or the card, so the Agent-turn card effect cannot fund that entry cost. One card can send only one Agent, using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents.’ Costs must be paid ‘before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played.’ A card with no Agent icons ‘may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you may deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 of the 4 already in your garrison, for a maximum of 5. At a non-Combat space you do not deploy units. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube icon recruits a troop ‘from your supply’ to your garrison. At a Combat space, deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn … plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. To Infiltrate an occupied space, recall your Spy from a connected post, which lets your Agent use that space. Gather Intelligence is available whenever you send an Agent: recall a connected Spy to draw a card, choosing immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence; on some spaces, two different Spies can be used for the two effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon permits sending to a connected space and ‘you do not recall the Spy for this.’ Infiltrate recalls a Spy to ignore an opponent's Agent. Gather Intelligence is chosen ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects).’ ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both.’

answers.answer: Your strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict cannot play Combat Intrigue, since only players with at least one unit may do so.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; if the last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. Combat: only each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict’ may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not stop you from playing Combat Intrigue again if an opponent plays after you. The window closes when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve once players pass ‘consecutively.’ After rewards, troops return to supply and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: With two players tied for first in a four-player game, each gets the second reward, nobody wins the Conflict, and nobody takes the Conflict card; the remaining players compete for the third reward. With two tied for first in a three-player game, each gets the second reward and no other rewards are given. A player with zero strength gets no reward in either case.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players each gain the second reward and ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; with four players, exactly two tied for first leave remaining players to compete for the third. With three or fewer players no other rewards are given. A player with ‘0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; additional sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward offers 3 spice to gain 1 VP, the doubled option lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP or pay 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘if you have one or more sandworms … double the rewards’; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. The example says you may pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply, check for a matching battle icon among your other face-up Conflict or Objective cards. If there is a match, you must flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild battle icon may match any of the three icon types in your supply, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the Conflict card, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card with the same icon; if present, you ‘must flip the matching pair face down.’ During Endgame the wild icon matches any of the three.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP, which is lost if you drop below 2. Reaching 4 gives the track bonus, which is retained if you later drop below 4. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance token and its VP; tying that player at 4 does not take it, since the token passes only when an opponent rises to a higher space.
answers.evidence: Scoring: 2 Influence = 1 VP, lost below 2; the 4 Influence bonus is not given back below 4. The Alliance token passes if an opponent rises to a ‘higher space’ on the track.

answers.answer: Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects during your Reveal turn. It can be pooled from multiple sources to buy one card or split from one source among different cards. After buying a Row card, its replacement is available immediately if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn allows Persuasion ‘before, between, or after’ Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards says Persuasion may be pooled or split, a replacement may be acquired after the Row card, and the acquired card goes face up into the discard pile.

answers.answer: At Makers, each Maker space without an Agent gets 1 spice in its bonus spot; when you send an Agent there, you gain all bonus spice there. A Maker Hooks icon lets you take a token from the bank if you do not already have one, and the token on your garrison is usually a requirement for summoning a worm. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while it remains on the board. A sandworm is taken from the bank and placed directly in your Conflict quadrant; it can never go in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: unoccupied Maker spaces receive 1 spice and an Agent gains all bonus spice there. Sandworms: Maker Hooks token is a usual requirement; the worm goes in the Conflict and ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ Shield Wall protects the three named locations.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. Ties are broken in order by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory: ‘At the end of a round’ the threshold or empty deck triggers Endgame; first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then most VP wins; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: flip 2 face up on the board and place the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 additional Intrigue cards and 4 additional Imperium cards to their respective decks. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contracts with contrasting backs are specifically for use with Rise of Ix, so they are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: 20 contracts, 2 face up and 18 face down; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 additional Imperium cards into the decks; Shaddam is an option. Components and the Rise of Ix subsection identify the contrasting-back 10 as used specifically with Rise of Ix.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a contract from the bank flipped face up; if all contracts have been taken, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when you send an Agent to a Maker space and gain the required amount of spice that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: the contract icon takes one face-up contract and replaces it from the bank; when all are taken it ‘reverts to giving 2 Solari.’ Completion descriptions define Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space where you already sent your Agent that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip the token face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM completion: if you take a contract involving a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ wait until a future turn because you must have had the contract when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.

answers.answer: Unsupported by the supplied summary. It only says one- or two-player games require the separate Rivals rules supplement; it gives no standard two-player Rival count, Ornithopter Objective or First Player assignment, turn order, or whether a Rival Reveals.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘Games for one or two players require the separate Rivals rules supplement’; no Rival setup or turn procedure is summarized.

answers.answer: Unsupported by the supplied summary. It provides no Rival rules for an occupied-space reveal, Place Spy cards, applicable costs or effects, an empty House Hagal deck, or Reshuffle.
answers.evidence: Overview says one- or two-player games require the separate Rivals rules supplement, and explicitly notes that the rulebook does not detail those modes. No House Hagal procedures appear in the summary.
